purpose: Begin post-coverage multiplicity sampling by revisiting sparse or prior-NO_HIT states and recording newly discovered authoritative CVE/security namespaces without changing any physical evidence classifications.

policy.rule: 208/208 baseline coverage is a floor, not a stopping condition. Additional exact occurrences are retained to estimate target- and namespace-specific collision propensity with zero automatic physical-evidence weight.
policy.promotion: A newly discovered CVE or other identifier can supersede a prior revisable NO_HIT raw observation but cannot promote the state to P1/P2; physical evidence still requires independently verified physical semantics and provenance.
policy.temporal: NO_HIT records are historical query observations and remain in the append-only chain even when later searches discover exact occurrences.

records.context: RealDefense SUPERAntiSpyware local privilege escalation through an exposed dangerous function in SAS Core Service

libgit2 git_index_add heap corruption/use-after-free leading to potential arbitrary code execution; patched in 1.6.5 and 1.7.2

information_updates.finding: Post-coverage revisits demonstrate that a prior NO_HIT is query-time state, not a permanent property: 14494, 24577, 39532, 44940, 45779, 47275, 47957, 49401, 53242, 53999, 57796 and 63999 now have authoritative security namespaces.
information_updates.claims_boundary: Discovery of metadata collisions changes raw collision density only; it does not alter physical evidence status.

information_updates.finding: The security cases broaden the trust-boundary corpus across Git/index parsing, capability sandboxes, log confidentiality, filesystem parsing, session-cookie authentication, Unicode path equivalence, digital-manufacturing file parsers, mobile-analysis uploads and hardcoded cryptographic keys.
information_updates.claims_boundary: These are cross-domain hardening inputs, not Glob-number evidence.
